chunks: From him, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the found object (luqata), so he showed me a ring in his hand made of silver, saying, 'Indeed, this is from what the flood brought, and I intend to give it in charity.'

key_terms.اللُّقَطَة: Found property or lost object picked up by someone

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on found property (luqata) according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling of *luqata* (found property) by displaying a silver ring brought by a flood, indicating that the finder may retain possession with the intention of eventual charity. This example underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that found items, once properly identified and safeguarded, can be disposed of in charity if the owner does not claim them, reflecting the practical application of hadith regarding lost goods.
